identity.name: Session Manager
identity.oneLine: Electron desktop cockpit for driving Claude Code CLI sessions across projects via a TAB→Epic→PRD hierarchy, with scheduling, chat/terminal views, and mobile relay.
identity.claim: A local cockpit for Claude Code.
identity.sub: Terminal + 25+ config/observability/scheduling tabs (Settings, Skills, Hooks, MCP Servers, Tasks, Plans, History, Scheduler, Memory, Permissions, etc.), plus a mobile web cockpit at bilko.run. Runs on your machine — the fs layer never writes outside the home directory, and Project Pages ship with zero network egress.
identity.audience: For developers running Claude Code CLI sessions across multiple projects

pillars.d: A Terminal tab is anchored to one cwd; that cwd IS the project identity, and every skill, hook and permission scopes itself to it automatically.
status: 'proposed' is the human approval gate — an agent files a proposed Epic instead of writing into a feedback inbox; nothing runs until a human presses Approve & start.

pillars.t: A scheduler that respects the billing window
pillars.d: Approved PRDs run as claude -p jobs from a ≤3-deep machine-wide session slot pool, auto-pausing on rate-limit and resuming at the next 5h reset.

pillars.t: Single-writer law over the ops root
pillars.d: Every session-manager-operations/<namespace> folder has exactly one owning surface that may write it — fail-closed, enforced in opsOwnership.cjs.

feature.name: PRD ↔ Epic Communication (Verdict Routing)
feature.oneLine: Closes the loop between a scheduler job and the Epic that authored its PRD — the Epic's own validation verdict, not the job's self-report, is what the traffic light and retry logic trust.
feature.problem: A PRD check-in used to let the executor assert its own 'done' status, and the Scheduler's traffic light had no reliable way to reflect what the authoring Epic actually thought of that outcome — jobs could look green while the Epic that requested them was still unresolved, and a retry could re-run against a stale or archived PRD path.
feature.solution: A PRD check-in now triggers Epic validation instead of asserting done (PRD 986); the traffic light reads that validation verdict directly off the Epic (PRD 987); verifyRun resolves a PRD's path through a live-then-archived fallback so a retry can't target a dead path (PRD 991); and the executor prompt now frames the context digest so the PRD stays the task while the finish protocol stays last.

steps.d: PRD 984 — composeExecutorPrompt frames the context digest for the executor before the task itself.
PRD 986 — a PRD check-in triggers Epic validation and never asserts 'done' on its own.
PRD 987 — the Scheduler's traffic light reads the Epic's own validation verdict rather than the job's self-report.
PRD 991 — verifyRun's prdPath now resolves through live-then-archived, so a retry can't chase a path that's already been archived.
The executor prompt was reordered so the PRD is the task and the finish protocol stays last, not interleaved.

rules.t: A check-in triggers validation, never asserts done
rules.d: PRD 986 — the executor reporting completion is a request for review, not a verdict.

rules.t: The traffic light shows the Epic's verdict, not the job's claim

rules.t: Never credit a sibling job's commit to a no-op run
rules.d: PRD 983 — commit-guard checks stop a no-op run from inheriting another job's real work.

faq.a: The check-in triggers Epic validation (PRD 986); the Scheduler's traffic light then reflects that Epic's verdict (PRD 987) rather than the job asserting its own success.

faq.q: What stopped a retry from targeting a dead PRD path?
faq.a: verifyRun now resolves prdPath through a live-then-archived fallback (PRD 991), so an already-archived PRD is still found correctly.

architecture.summary: An Electron main process owns the claude CLI session pool, the scheduler queue and the fs layer; a React renderer talks to it only over typed, zod-validated IPC channels — neither side touches the other's concern directly.

principles.d: Every session-manager-operations/<namespace> has exactly one owning surface; a write by an undeclared writer throws (opsOwnership.cjs, fail-closed).
All fs writes go through config.cjs's writeJson/writeTextAtomic (tmp + rename) — no ad hoc fs.writeFile in app-owned state.
Renderer zustand stores never cross-subscribe; components compose multiple stores via hooks/selectors instead.
A tab IS a cwd; every nav destination, skill and permission derives from the focused project, not global config.

brief.purpose: A local Electron cockpit for orchestrating Claude Code CLI sessions across projects, organizing work into Agent+Tag-grounded Epics that decompose into scheduler-run PRDs.
what: The **TAB→EPIC→PRD** hierarchy is the whole app's spine: a Terminal tab pins a project cwd, each **Epic** is a `PromptSession` combining an **Agent** persona (who) and a **Tag** mission (what), and Epics author `session-manager-operations/scheduler/` PRDs that headless `claude -p` jobs execute under a 3-slot concurrency cap.

Recent work (`295c875`, `8bac5b0`, `f5d3878`) rebuilt the **Chat view** to read directly from the `~/.claude/projects/.../*.jsonl` transcript feed via typed per-event-family renderers, demoting `chatRunner.cjs` to a live tap rather than the source of truth — this replaced a 500-entry ring buffer with an indexed, paged read.

The **Agent + Tag** vocabulary was formalized as the per-Epic customization layer (`d7c5d47`, `6b6a092`, `0c294fe`): Settings.json stays substrate-only (identical for every Epic in a project), while `model`/behavior differences belong to a custom Agent persona or Tag, not a Settings edit.

**Project Home** (`ca3d82a`, `a34da4b`, `2402369`) shifted to hosting a generated `home.html` document with a single "generate" action pulling from a saved component library, rather than juggling separate pages.

The **Keybindings tab was fully deleted** (`e0f779a`) as dead-clean-up work, and several open discussion Epics (parallelism gaps, PRD↔Epic communication, Agent vs Skill responsibility) remain unresolved design questions rather than shipped features.

scope.text: Agent-facing Epic-proposal channels (/propose-epic, RCA auto-filed Epics, feedback sweep) are removed; only a human pressing New Epic can mint one — SINGLE-CREATOR LAW enforced fail-closed in epicMint.cjs
Scheduler reframed as a browser over TAB→EPIC→PRD; flat scheduler/prds/ retired in favor of per-Epic scheduler/epics/<epic-id>/prds/
Keybindings tab and all its surfaces deleted entirely
Chat now sources its transcript from the JSONL feed with typed per-event renderers instead of chatRunner as source of truth
classifyLine now emits an array of events per line instead of one, fixing dropped transcript events
Settings (System/Project/Local) is substrate only; per-Epic behavior differences must be a Tag, an Agent persona, or a future effort/reasoning PRD — never a Settings edit

conventions: Zustand stores are isolated islands (config.ts, live.ts, voice.ts, scheduleState.ts, toast.ts) — never cross-subscribe; compose in components.
Never return a freshly-built value (`?? []`, `.filter()`, `.map()`) from a zustand selector — causes React #185 blank-app; select raw slice and derive after.
All fs writes go through config.cjs's atomic writeJson/writeTextAtomic with a declared `writer` per the single-writer law over session-manager-operations/ namespaces.
Cap at 3 concurrent `claude -p` processes machine-wide (scheduler + chat runs share one session-slot pool) — exceeding this OOM-killed Electron once already.
No CommonJS in renderer, no ES modules in main; `.cjs` files bypass the package's `type: module`.
